newsitem.title: UK: BT -- from privatisation to global power.
newsitem.headline: BT -- from privatisation to global power.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc, which on Sunday sealed a ground-breaking merger with MCI Communications Corp, has matured into a major force in the global communications industry since privatisation in 1984.
Following are some of the key dates in its development:
1984 - Privatised under Margaret Thatcher's Conservative government. Issue helps to transform image of share ownership as millions of small investors buy into BT.
1985 - Faces first serious competitive challenge in the UK with the launch of Cable & Wireless Plc's Mercury Communications
1985 - Launches Cellnet radio telephone in a joint venture with Securicor. 1988 - Acquires 22 percent of mobile phone company McCaw Cellular Communications Inc for $1.5 billion
1991 - Government sells off remaining 48 pct British Telecommunications Plc (BT) stake.
1992 - BT wins licence from the German goverment to offer satellite services, adding to its existing satellite operations in France and the Netherlands.
1993 - Announces a multi-million pound, five-year contract to provide a communications network to improve Europe's air traffic management.
1993 - Pays $4.3 billion to take a 20 percent stake in MCI Communications Corp.
1993 - Joins forces with Banco Santander SA of Spain to sell a range of voice and data services.
1994 - Creates Concert Communications Co, a $1 billion joint venture with MCI to provide global corporate communciation services using IT technology.
1994 - Forms alliance with Danish, Finish and Norwegian firms as part of push into Scandinavia.
1995 - Announces joint venture with Italy's Banca Nazionale del Lavoro to target business customers.
March - buys 25 percent stake in Clear Communications, New Zealand's second biggest telecoms company.
May - breaks off merger talks with British rival Cable & Wireless Plc
June - announces 200 million stg investment in internet venture with MCI.
July - forms computer networking and on-line services joint venture with Microsoft Corp
Sept - takes 25 percent stake in Cegetel, new French telecoms consortium led by Compagnie Generale des Eaux for 1.1 billion stg and the share capital of BT France.
Oct - enters Hungarian telecoms market.
- confirms intends to bid for a Dutch telecoms licence
- says would seek a new telecoms partner in Germany
after RWE AG RWE.F quit alliance with BT and Viag.
Nov 3 - confirms it will merge with MCI to create Concert Plc, the world's second largest telecoms group with annual revenue of over 25 billion pounds.
